body.heading: The part you never see
paragraphs: Someone holds a door for a stranger who is having a rough morning. That stranger is a little less sharp with the next person they meet. Nobody traces it back. Kindness mostly works like that: quietly, and out of sight.

There is even a name for the warm lift you get from doing good — a helper's high. But the echo goes further than your own mood. People who receive kindness tend to pass some of it on, and the chain can run for links you will never hear about.

body.heading: Why it matters on ordinary days
paragraphs: You cannot control whether your kindness gets noticed, thanked, or returned. You can only control whether it happens. Most days, that is enough of a job.
And once in a while the echo comes back years later, in a sentence that starts 'You probably don't remember, but...' Those sentences are worth more than any round of applause.

description: You rarely see where a kind act ends up — but it travels further than you think.
